title: Message Passing in GNNs
interviewAnswer: GNN layers aggregate information from neighbors and combine it with the current node representation. Repeating layers expands the receptive field over graph hops.
why: Message passing is the core abstraction behind many GNNs and explains how local graph structure becomes learned node representations.
intuition: Each node receives summaries from neighbors, combines them with its own state, and repeats this for several layers so information travels multiple hops.
deepDive: A generic layer computes messages from neighbors, aggregates them with a permutation-invariant function such as sum/mean/max, then updates the node representation. After k layers, a node typically depends on k-hop neighborhoods. Too many layers can lead to over-smoothing or over-squashing; high-degree neighborhoods may require sampling.
workedExample: In reviewer recommendation, a developer embedding can incorporate the PRs they reviewed; another layer can indirectly incorporate relationships from nearby developers/PRs.
commonMistakes: Thinking neighbor order should affect a permutation-invariant graph aggregator.
Adding many layers without considering oversmoothing.
Ignoring edge features/types when they carry semantics.
followUps: Why must aggregation be permutation invariant?
How many hops does k layers see?
production: Bound neighborhood expansion for memory/latency and monitor degree skew; giant hubs can dominate compute and representation quality.
